result.summary: The image shows a narrow urban street with sidewalks on both sides and parallel parking on the right. While the narrow roadway likely encourages lower vehicle speeds, the environment lacks marked pedestrian crossings and clear sightlines at potential crossing points.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction
hazards.description: Parked vehicles along the right side of the street block sightlines between pedestrians on the sidewalk and approaching drivers.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the roadway where cars are parked

hazards.name: Lack of Marked Crossings
hazards.description: There are no visible marked crosswalks at the intersection ahead, forcing pedestrians to cross in unmarked areas.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces closest to the intersection to improve visibility for both pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: Marked Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install high-visibility marked crosswalks at the intersection to clearly define pedestrian right-of-way.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install curb extensions at the intersection to shorten the crossing distance and place pedestrians in a more visible position before they step into the street.

result.summary: The image shows a narrow urban street with a mix of residential and commercial buildings. A paved sidewalk is present but narrow, directly abutting the buildings and separated from the roadway by a curb and a lane of parallel-parked vehicles.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction from Parked Vehicles
hazards.description: Parked cars along the curb block the line of sight between pedestrians on the sidewalk and drivers on the roadway, particularly near the gated alleyway.
hazards.location_in_image: Foreground and mid-ground along the curb line.

hazards.name: Narrow Pedestrian Clear Zone
hazards.description: The sidewalk width is constrained by building frontages and stairs, which may hinder accessibility for some users.
hazards.location_in_image: Along the building line on the left and center.

interventions.title: Daylighting at Alley Entrance
interventions.description: Restrict parking immediately adjacent to the gated alleyway to improve sightlines for both pedestrians and drivers exiting the alley.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk at potential crossing points or the alley entrance to reduce crossing distance and improve pedestrian visibility.

result.summary: The environment features a two-lane street with sidewalks on both sides and a marked continental-style crosswalk at the intersection. However, the lack of traffic calming measures and the presence of on-street parking create potential visibility hazards for pedestrians.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction from Parked Vehicles
hazards.description: Parallel parked cars on the left side of the street can obscure pedestrians, particularly children, from the view of oncoming drivers.

hazards.name: Lack of Traffic Calming
hazards.description: The straight roadway design without physical speed controls may encourage vehicle speeds that are unsafe for a mixed-use area.
hazards.location_in_image: Main travel lanes extending toward the background.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk into the parking lane at the intersection to shorten the crossing distance and improve visibility between pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces immediately adjacent to the crosswalk to ensure clear sightlines for all road users.

interventions.title: Speed Humps or Tables
interventions.description: Install physical traffic calming measures to reduce vehicle speeds along this residential/commercial block.

result.summary: The image depicts a residential street with a continuous concrete sidewalk and brick row houses. While the walkway is wide, it shows signs of wear with visible cracks and a building entrance railing that slightly narrows the clear path.

hazards.name: Uneven Pavement
hazards.description: Visible cracking and minor heaving in the concrete sidewalk slabs in the foreground.
hazards.location_in_image: Bottom center and right foreground sidewalk area

hazards.name: Fixed Obstruction
hazards.description: A metal railing and stairs for a building entrance protrude into the sidewalk's clear width.
hazards.location_in_image: Left side of the image, attached to the red and brick building

interventions.title: Sidewalk Repair
interventions.description: Patch or replace cracked concrete slabs to ensure a smooth, trip-free walking surface.

interventions.title: Clear Path Maintenance
interventions.description: Ensure that building appurtenances like railings maintain a minimum clear walking width of at least 4 feet per ADA standards.
